answer: One concrete defense is costly, non-transferable reputation: an agent earns standing only by completing verified work over time, like a vine that grows strong by climbing slowly. Spawning thousands of fakes gains nothing, because each identity must separately pay that time and effort cost before it can transact. Peer audits act like a falcon scanning a field, flagging clusters of identical behavior for stake slashing. Like yarrow, which spreads only where its roots truly take hold, influence should follow sustained, checkable contribution, so fakes cost more than they can extract.
